For progress claims, capture claimedToDate, previouslyCertified and thisClaim separately - do not add them together. retentionPercent and retentionAmount are the retention withheld; set both to 0 only if the document explicitly shows no retention. lienWaiverAttached is true only if a lien waiver, statutory declaration or release is actually referenced in the document. parameters.content:
## Sample client: Braewick Construction Group (fictional)

Processes construction invoices automatically. Handles two kinds, each checked differently:
- **Progress payments** - subcontractors bill in stages as work gets done
- **Material and equipment invoices**

**Setup needed**

**Google Sheets** - a file named "AP Invoice Automation" with two tabs:
- Audit Log: invoiceKey, vendorName, invoiceNumber, poNumber, jobNumber, costCode, claimType, totalAmount, retentionAmount, netPayable, riskFlags, outcome, processedAt, executionId
- Error Log: failedAt, workflowName, failedNode, errorMessage, executionUrl, executionId
Connect a Google Sheets credential (Drive or Calendar logins won't work).

**Airtable** - two tables:
- Purchase Orders: poNumber, vendorName, poAmount, status, qboAccountId (QuickBooks expense account ID)
- Goods Receipts (delivery records): poNumber, receivedAmount, receivedDate, status

**QuickBooks** - connect a credential on both QuickBooks steps. Vendor names on invoices must match the vendor's display name in QuickBooks. The bill is entered at the amount to pay, after retention is held back.

**Errors** - already wired: Settings > Error Workflow points at this workflow. Re-select it if you import a copy.

**Per-email runs** - **Hand Each Email To Its Own Run** calls this same workflow by ID. If you import a copy, point it at the copy.

## How invoices are checked

**Materials and equipment** - the invoice, purchase order (PO) and delivery record must all agree, within 2%.

**Progress payments, change orders, final payments** - there's no delivery record, so the numbers must add up instead:
- Total billed so far can't exceed the contract value
- Total billed so far minus what was already approved must equal this bill
- Retention (a % held back until the job is finished) must be applied
- A lien waiver (the subcontractor's signed release) must be attached

This is where construction companies actually lose money: paying for the same work twice, paying in full when some should be held back, or paying without a signed release.

parameters.content:
## 1 · Receive the invoice

Every 5 minutes, checks Gmail for unread emails with a PDF attached. **Each email is handed to its own run** of this workflow, so two invoices arriving together are both processed and one waiting for approval never holds up the next.

Emails without a PDF are ignored. If the PDF is a scanned image with no readable text, the team gets a Slack alert instead of the AI receiving a blank page.

## 2 · Skip duplicates

**Check 1 (before AI):** each email gets an ID (email ID + file name), checked against the Invoice Log so a reprocessed email costs nothing.

**Check 2 (after AI):** vendor + invoice number is checked against invoices already **posted**. This catches the same invoice re-sent in a new email. Rejected invoices can be resubmitted.

Both searches always continue when nothing is found - no match means it's new.

Note: Google Sheets can't block duplicates by itself, so two copies arriving at the exact same moment could both get through.

## 3 · AI reads the invoice

The AI pulls out: vendor, invoice and PO numbers, job number, cost code, invoice type, amount billed so far, amount already approved, retention, and whether a lien waiver is attached.

It's told never to make up a PO, job number or amount, and to keep each billing figure separate - otherwise the math check later is useless.

## 4 · Compare with records

If the AI isn't sure it read the invoice correctly, a person checks it in Slack first. **Looks correct** continues; **Stop** ends the run so the invoice can be entered manually.

The invoice is then compared with the purchase order and delivery record in Airtable. If either is missing, the invoice still continues and is flagged for review instead of silently stopping.

Both lookups retry automatically if Airtable is briefly unavailable.

## 5 · Approval

Invoices with any issue → AP specialist reviews. Clean invoices → budget owner approves. Clean invoices move fast; only problems need extra attention.

Both approvals happen in Slack, and the workflow waits up to 2 days for an answer.

**No answer in 2 days is not a rejection** - it gets its own alert and is logged as *no_decision*.

## 6 · Add to QuickBooks & log

The expense account comes from the PO's **qboAccountId**. If there is no PO or no account, the approved bill is not posted and the team is asked to enter it by hand.

The vendor is then looked up in QuickBooks by display name. If it isn't found, the bill is not added and the team gets a Slack alert.

QuickBooks gets the **amount to pay** (after retention is held back), not the full invoice total.

Every invoice is saved to the Invoice Log - posted, rejected, no_decision, vendor missing or no account. Every path ends by marking the email as read.

## 7 · If something breaks

This branch runs whenever a live run fails. It works because the workflow is its own error workflow (**Settings > Error Workflow = this workflow**). If you import or duplicate it, select the copy there again. Manual test runs don't trigger it.

It posts a Slack alert and logs the error to the Error Log tab. The alert says whether the bill could already be in QuickBooks.

**The failed invoice is not retried automatically** - the Gmail check only looks at new emails. Process it manually from the link in the alert.
